title: Add TypeScript types + docs for route-level quantization profile settings and compatibility errors
author: Ibrahim Khan
release_notes: - Type-safe route-level quantization profile settings (quantization_profile_ref) for Console/control-plane parity. - New error shapes for compatibility failures with actionable remediation fields. - Docs/examples for enabling/disabling per route and handling incompatibility responses.
body: Summary: This PR adds first-class TypeScript types for route-level quantization profile settings and the structured errors returned by compatibility checks when users attempt to enable an incompatible profile for a given route/model/hardware/context regime. It also updates the SDK docs and examples to show how to (1) set quantization_profile_ref on a route, (2) preview/validate changes, and (3) handle compatibility errors in a user-friendly way. Context: Control plane now supports opt-in per-route enablement of quantization profiles (Quantization Profile Library). Customers and Console workflows rely on compatibility guardrails; the SDK should expose these fields in a type-safe way so integrators can build their own automation/approval flows. Changes included: 1) New route quantization types: - Added QuantizationProfileRef and RouteQuantizationSettings to model quantization_profile_ref as a constrained string union with a safe escape hatch for forward-compatibility: type QuantizationProfileRef = 'default' | `profile:${string}` | `alias:${'recommended' | 'latest'}` | (string & { __brand?: 'QuantizationProfileRef' }); - Added RouteUpdateInput.quantization_profile_ref?: QuantizationProfileRef and Route.quantization_profile_ref?: QuantizationProfileRef in the generated/client-side types. - Added helper guards/parsers in utils/quantization.ts: isQuantizationProfileRef(), parseQuantProfileRef() (best-effort parsing for logging/UX). 2) Compatibility error typing (API error surface): - Introduced QuantizationCompatibilityErrorDetails and QuantizationCompatibilityErrorReason to represent server-provided reasons: MODEL_MISMATCH, PROFILE_DEPRECATED, GPU_UNSUPPORTED, PRECISION_UNSUPPORTED, MAX_CONTEXT_EXCEEDED, SEQ_LEN_DISTRIBUTION_UNSAFE, TENANT_POLICY_BLOCKED, KILL_SWITCH_ENABLED. - Added an explicit error code union for control-plane config writes: type RouteConfigErrorCode = 'QUANT_PROFILE_INCOMPATIBLE' | 'QUANT_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND' | 'QUANT_PROFILE_FORBIDDEN' | 'RBAC_DENIED' | 'VALIDATION_ERROR' | ... - Updated RedwoodError typing to expose error.code and error.details for 409 responses from route config endpoints, without breaking existing catch blocks. 3) Docs + examples: - Added docs snippet showing enabling a profile per route: set quantization_profile_ref: 'profile:qp_llama3_70b_int8_v3' and rollback to 'default'. - Added example for handling incompatibility (409): printing error.details.reason + remediation (e.g., "switch to a supported GPU tier", "reduce max_context", or "use default precision"). - Added note on alias semantics: alias:recommended/latest may change over time; best practice is to pin profile:* for production after evaluation. 4) Tests/validation: - Added unit tests for parseQuantProfileRef and for error narrowing in __tests__/errors.quantization.test.ts. - Updated OpenAPI snapshot fixtures used by the SDK generator to include quantization_profile_ref on Route and compatibility error examples for PATCH /v1/routes/{route_id}. Implementation notes / compatibility: - Non-breaking: all new fields are optional and default behavior remains unchanged when quantization_profile_ref is omitted or set to 'default'. - Forward-compatibility: QuantizationProfileRef includes a branded string fallback so new server-side ref formats won’t hard-break TypeScript builds. - Aligns with Console backend behavior: server still performs determinism + compatibility checks; SDK types only surface the settings and returned diagnostics. Follow-ups: - If we finalize alias support semantics (recommended/latest) for GA, we should add a short section in the public docs site linking to the compatibility matrix (tracked elsewhere). - Consider adding a dedicated error class (QuantProfileIncompatibleError) once we see usage patterns in design partner integrations.
commits: feat(errors): add compatibility error details + code union for route config writes
docs(examples): enable quant profile per route + handle incompatibility responses
test: add parsing + error narrowing tests for quant profile refs
chore: update OpenAPI fixtures for route quantization fields
conversation: Monica Patel (review): Can we avoid a hard union that will break if the server changes the ref format? Suggest adding a branded string escape hatch or parser helper so customers can still compile if a new prefix lands.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Good call — added (string & { __brand?: 'QuantizationProfileRef' }) to the union and added parseQuantProfileRef() for best-effort UX/logging. Updated docs to recommend pinning profile:* for prod.

Benji Okafor (review): Please align error codes with what control plane emits. For incompatibility we should key off QUANT_PROFILE_INCOMPATIBLE (409) and include a typed reason enum; avoid reusing generic VALIDATION_ERROR for this case.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Updated RouteConfigErrorCode union + added QuantizationCompatibilityErrorReason enum. Also updated OpenAPI fixtures with the 409 example response so generated docs stay consistent.
Jordan Lee (review): Small ask: make sure 'alias:latest' doesn’t encourage silent changes. Can we add a doc warning that aliases can move and customers should pin for audited rollouts?
Ibrahim Khan (author): Added explicit warning in docs/routes.md and in example comments; also included guidance to use audit logs/change control in production.
Monica Patel (approval): Looks good. Thanks for the forward-compat escape hatch + clearer remediation guidance.
